_meta.title: Total tax revenue as a share of GDP, OECD comparison
_meta.source: OECD Revenue Statistics 2025, United States country note, 2024 preliminary data
notes: This counts ALL levels of government: federal, state and local. That is why 25.6% is higher than the 17.2% federal-only figure from CBO. The two are not interchangeable and any chart must say which it uses.
US peak was 28.3% in 2000; low was 22.9% in 2009.
The US is the only OECD member with no value-added tax, which accounts for most of the gap.
2024 is the latest OECD year. It breaks the 1995/2025 convention used elsewhere; say so.
